_comments._how_to_use: Copy this file, fill in EVERY value with a non-negative number, and COMMIT the filled file BEFORE the run. analyze_accuracy.py refuses any null unless --exploratory is given. No value here is a recommendation: none is suggested on purpose, because a threshold chosen after seeing the data is not a threshold.
_comments.cpu_bias_abs_max_pp: Largest allowed |mean(sender CPU % - reference CPU %)| in any steady-state phase, in percentage points of total capacity.
_comments.cpu_mae_max_pp: Largest allowed mean absolute error of sender CPU % against the reference, per phase, in percentage points.
_comments.cpu_p95_abs_error_max_pp: Largest allowed 95th-percentile (nearest-rank) absolute CPU error per phase, in percentage points.
_comments.memory_bias_abs_max_pp: Largest allowed |mean(sender memory % - reference memory %)| per phase, in percentage points of MemTotal.
_comments.memory_mae_max_pp: Largest allowed mean absolute memory error per phase, in percentage points.
_comments.memory_p95_abs_error_max_pp: Largest allowed 95th-percentile absolute memory error per phase, in percentage points.
_comments.frequency_bias_abs_max_khz: Largest allowed |mean(sender kHz - reference kHz)| per phase, applied to EACH reference (cpuinfo_cur_freq and vcgencmd) separately.
_comments.frequency_mae_max_khz: Largest allowed mean absolute frequency error per phase, in kHz, per reference.
_comments.frequency_p95_abs_error_max_khz: Largest allowed 95th-percentile absolute frequency error per phase, in kHz, per reference.
_comments.temperature_bias_abs_max_c: Largest allowed |mean(sender deg C - reference deg C)| per phase, applied to EACH reference (sysfs and vcgencmd) separately. The sysfs reference is the same file as the sender's, so it only checks the read path.
_comments.temperature_mae_max_c: Largest allowed mean absolute temperature error per phase, in degrees C, per reference.
_comments.temperature_p95_abs_error_max_c: Largest allowed 95th-percentile absolute temperature error per phase, in degrees C, per reference.
_comments.cpu_reference_vs_stimulus_abs_max_pp: Largest allowed |reference CPU % - achieved stimulus duty| per phase, in percentage points: checks the reference against the load generator's own measurement of what it produced.
_comments.memory_reference_vs_stimulus_abs_max_mib: Largest allowed |reference memory growth - stimulus VmRSS growth| per mem phase, in MiB.
_comments.max_cpu_edge_gap_ms: A CPU window is EXCLUDED (and counted) if either of its edges had to be interpolated across a reference gap wider than this, in milliseconds. Use a value at least as large as the reference interval, or ordinary windows are dropped.
_comments.max_instant_distance_1hz_ms: A memory / frequency / temperature comparison against a 1 Hz reference (/proc/meminfo, cpuinfo_cur_freq, thermal_zone0) is EXCLUDED (and counted) if the nearest reference record is further away than this, in milliseconds.
_comments.max_instant_distance_10s_ms: The same for the 10 s vcgencmd references (frequency and temperature). Their records are 10 s apart, so a limit below half that interval (5 s) excludes some pairs by construction.
_comments.step_response_pi_clock_max_ms: Largest allowed time from a phase start to the first sender message past the step midpoint, on the Pi clock, in milliseconds (CPU and memory). A phase whose plateau is never reached fails.
_comments.step_response_twin_visible_max_ms: Same, but as seen at Ditto (patched_at minus the clock offset). Reported N/A for a dry run, which has no patched_at, but it must still be pre-registered.
_comments.min_samples_per_phase: Smallest allowed number of comparison samples (n) in a phase; fewer fails that phase. A count of messages, not a duration.
